findings: Every frame of 80 ms or more coincides with new pipelines (max 542 ms with 16). The frame worker spends 36% of those windows in wait_pipeline_impl.
The startup prewarm compiles 12,473 pipelines in 3.3 s (all Dawn blob cache hits, DXC); each new room still adds 10-48.

skip_unready_pipelines=true had no effect: begin_frame(clearEfb=false) sets g_requirePersistentEfbPipelines and persistent texture copies set requireReadyPipelines, so Prime passes wait without limit. This is by design, to avoid losing EFB copy contents.
Game thread: 0x803E9F78 waits on the previous frame's GPU work (250 ms timeout), reading OSGetTime in a loop. That is idle time; PPC_Mftb is not an optimization target.
Game thread busy time, excluding that wait: 66-68% game code. Call-boundary interrupt poll about 10.5%, GPU FIFO word writes about 8%, indirect dispatch about 4%.
changes: os_interrupt.cpp OS_HLE_PollPendingPrimeIpcInterrupt: full device checks on every 8th translated call return (thread_local counter); the idle loop (0x804E6D20) still checks on every pass. The CP breakpoint gate now runs on every checked poll.
prime_cpu_fifo_capture.h Capture::Push: whole-word fast path inside a burst. Validation, byte order and commit semantics unchanged.
memory.cpp PrimeGpuTryCaptureCpuFifo: acquire loads, inlined active check, no zero-init of the burst copy.
